sections.h2: Where is Grand Junction, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Grand Junction is a home rule city and the county seat of Mesa County, 247 miles west-southwest of Denver, and the largest city in Colorado outside the Front Range Urban Corridor. It is the economic and cultural center of the Western Slope.

The 2020 census counted 65,560 residents, which made it the 17th most populous municipality in the state, and the 2025 estimate shown on Wikipedia is 71,780. The city covers about 40 square miles at an elevation of 4,646 feet.

sections.h2: How did Grand Junction get its name and start?
sections.html:
The name refers to the junction of the Colorado River, once called the Grand River, with the Gunnison River. Before incorporation, the community was known as Ute.

The Ute people lived in the region before European-American farmers arrived in the 1880s. In September 1881 the former Ute Indian Territory was abolished and the Utes were moved to a reservation. George Addison Crawford incorporated the town on July 22, 1882. Railroads reached the city in 1882 from Pueblo by narrow gauge and in 1890 by standard gauge from New Castle.

Fruit growing became important by the late nineteenth century, especially between Grand Junction and Palisade, with peaches, pears, apricots, plums, cherries and grapes. Wineries opened in the area beginning in the late twentieth century.

sections.h2: What does the high desert climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Grand Junction has a cold semi-arid climate with hot summers and about 9 inches of precipitation a year, so roofs and exteriors face sun and heat more than rain.

  • July averages 78.2 degrees F, and January averages 27.4 degrees F.
  • About 68 days a year reach 90 degrees or higher, and about 8 days reach 100 degrees or higher.
  • The average last freeze is April 25 and the average first freeze is October 11.

Long stretches of heat are hard on air conditioners, roofing and exterior paint. A buyer's inspector will often check the cooling system and the roof, and a cash buyer prices what they find instead of asking you to repair it.

Health care, tourism, agriculture, livestock and energy are the main contributors, according to Wikipedia. The largest employers it lists give a sense of the job base.

Energy has a history of boom and bust here. Oil shale development lifted the area in the 1970s and early 1980s, and Exxon's withdrawal in 1982, known locally as Black Sunday, caused an economic bust.

sections.h2: Which schools and college are in Grand Junction?
sections.html:
Mesa County Valley School District 51 provides public K-12 education in the area. Wikipedia names Fruita Monument, Grand Junction, Central and Palisade high schools among its five, plus an R-5 High School.

Colorado Mesa University enrolls nearly 10,000 students and is the largest university in western Colorado. Owners of rentals near campus are one group that sometimes decides to sell.

sections.h2: What roads, rail and flights serve Grand Junction?
sections.html:
Interstate 70 links Grand Junction east to Glenwood Springs and Denver and west toward Green River, Utah. U.S. Highways 6 and 50 also meet in the city, and State Highway 340 runs through the Redlands to Fruita.

  • Grand Junction Regional Airport is the largest airport in western Colorado and the third largest in the state.
  • Amtrak's California Zephyr stops at Grand Junction Station.
  • Grand Valley Transit provides local buses, and Bustang offers intercity service.

The city sits in the Grand Valley, a river valley about 30 miles long. Nearby areas include the Redlands, Palisade, Fruita and Loma, and a buyer may compare a house in the city with homes in those communities.

sections.h2: Are short-term rentals regulated in Grand Junction?
sections.html:
Yes. Any property owner who plans to run a short-term rental inside city limits must get a license from the City of Grand Junction and renew it every year, under Ordinance No. 5163 adopted July 5, 2023.

The application fee is $275 per property. The city also caps how many residentially zoned lots can hold a primary short-term rental.

  • Downtown (North Ave to I-70B, Highway 50 to N 17th St): no more than 7 percent of residentially zoned lots.
  • Outside downtown: no more than 3 percent.
  • Lots with four or fewer units: one primary and one secondary rental allowed.
  • Lots with five or more units: no more than 10 percent of units.

If you own a house that has been run as a short-term rental, check whether the license is current before talking to a buyer, because the cap affects who can get a new license. Community Development is at 250 N 5th Street and can be reached at 970-244-1430. The city page does not say whether a license transfers on sale, so ask the office.

sections.h2: When are Mesa County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Mesa County's assessor lists the key dates: the Treasurer mails tax bills on January 31, the first installment is due February 28, full payment is due April 30 and the second installment is due June 15.

DateEvent
January 1Property is valued as of this date
January 31Treasurer mails tax bills
February 28First installment due
April 30Full-year payment due
May 1Real property valuation notices mailed
June 8Last day to file a real property protest
June 15Second installment due

If you sell between January and the payment dates, the tax for the prior year may still be unpaid, so the title company will want to see the balance.

sections.h2: What does the state charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
Colorado's documentary fee is one cent per $100 of consideration on a deed conveying real property, with any partial $100 counted as a full one. It is paid to the county clerk and recorder, and nothing is owed at $500 or less.

On a $300,000 sale that comes to $300. The contract usually names the party who pays it.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Grand Junction?
sections.html:
You contact us with the address and condition, we review it, and you get an offer you can accept or decline. A title company confirms ownership, orders the tax certificate and prepares the deed, and the deed is recorded in Mesa County.

There is no lender in the middle, so closing depends on title work and the date you choose. We do not promise a price or a timeline before we see the house.

faqs.q: What county is Grand Junction in?
faqs.a: Mesa County. Grand Junction is the county seat and the largest city in the county, so property taxes are billed by the Mesa County Treasurer and deeds are recorded in Mesa County.

faqs.q: When is the second property tax payment due in Mesa County?
faqs.a: June 15. The first installment is due February 28, and paying in full is due April 30, according to the Mesa County assessor's key dates page.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Grand Junction house short term?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires an annual short-term rental license with a $275 application fee per property, and it limits the share of residential lots that can have a primary short-term rental.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Grand Junction house without repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not have to fix the roof, cooling system or cosmetic items first. The offer reflects the condition.

faqs.q: How hot does Grand Junction get?
faqs.a: About 68 days a year reach 90 degrees F or higher, and about 8 days reach 100 or higher. That heat is why inspectors look closely at cooling systems and roofs.
